newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan state monopoly seeks Emirates oil stake.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan state monopoly seeks Emirates oil stake.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp was in talks with Crescent Oil Co of the United Arab Emirates to buy a 40 percent stake in a Crescent affiliate called BGOI, the economics ministry said on Monday.
The ministry, it a brief statement, said Chinese Petroleum had been invited by Crescent to buy a 40 percent stake of the affiliate. The economic ministry oversees the oil monopoly.

"The move is aimed at gaining control of Taiwan's oil sources and lowering import costs," the ministry said in the statement issued in Taipei on Monday, the last day of a five-day Chinese lunar new year holiday.
Ministry and monopoly officials could note be reached for comment. The statement gave few details, calling BGOI an oil company but giving no description of its operations.
The pending acquisition has Taiwan government approval.
"The project has been approved by the cabinet. Chinese Petroleum and Crescent will immediately discuss purchasing prices for the shares and finalise the deal," the ministry said.
Taiwan and its powerful export-driven economy are highly dependent on imported crude for energy, buying some 150 million barrels a year.

Taiwan's parliament, in approving Chinese Petroleum's budget on December 19, reduced or eliminated funding for a number of overseas investments as part of a drive to bring the firm under tighter state control before a planned privatisation.
